sections.heading: Default structure
sections.text: Buck is the simplest step-down converter. Prefer cascaded current-inner voltage-outer control. The inner loop regulates inductor current, providing fast current limiting and damping the LC resonance. Single-loop PI is feasible but gives slower transients.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: V_out = D*V_in. LC resonance: f_LC = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C)). Current-loop crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/5 to fsw/10. Voltage-loop crossover: f_cv < f_LC/3 for adequate phase margin. Inductor current ripple: delta_I = (V_in - V_out)*D/(L*fsw).

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: The buck has no RHPZ, so the voltage-loop bandwidth is limited only by the LC resonance and the switching frequency. The LC resonance peak must be damped — either by the current loop (cascaded) or by adding a zero in the voltage compensator (single-loop PI). ESR of the output capacitor dominates steady-state ripple.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If the buck cannot meet transient specs with a single PI, promote to cascaded current-mode. If the cascaded buck still cannot meet specs, the limitation is passive sizing (L, C) or the switching frequency — not the controller.
